headline: The Hutter Prize measures intelligence better than any OpenAI benchmark
summary: A 20-year-old contest offers cash rewards for compressing a Wikipedia XML dump, providing a more honest measure of intelligence than typical AI benchmarks by focusing on true algorithmic efficiency.
details: The Hutter Prize, a 20-year-old contest, offers cash rewards for compressing a Wikipedia XML dump without loss of information. Since 2020, competitors have been challenged to compress the 1-gigabyte file enwik9, providing a hard, indisputable number for compression efficiency.

Unlike many benchmarks, the Hutter Prize directly links good text compression to effective text prediction, arguing they are essentially the same. This approach aims to identify systems that learn faster, generalize from less data, and perform better, aligning with the goal of strong AI research.

A unique scoring rule combines the size of the compressed file with the size of the decompression program, preventing "cheating" by using massive pre-trained models. Competitors must also adhere to strict hardware limits: a single CPU core, under 10GB of RAM, and completion within 100 hours.

The current record, set on September 3, 2024, by Kaido Orav and Byron Knoll, compressed 1 billion bytes into 110,793,128 bytes (11.1% of original size). Their 1.585% improvement over the previous record earned them €7,950 from the prize's founder, Marcus Hutter.

This concept is gaining traction in mainstream AI research. A 2024 ICLR paper, "Language Modeling Is Compression," co-authored by Marcus Hutter and teams from Google DeepMind, Meta AI, and Inria, demonstrated that advanced models like Chinchilla 70B are indeed excellent compressors across text, images, and audio.

The CoRecursive podcast aptly summarized that "compression is the ultimate prediction test." While traditional benchmarks offer performance insights based on predefined questions, a compression ratio directly reflects a model's effectiveness in representing actual data distribution, offering a more truthful measure of intelligence.

headline: Meetily transcribes and summarizes meetings for free without a subscription
summary: This open-source tool offers real-time transcription and AI summaries for video calls on Windows and macOS, keeping your data local and private. It provides a powerful alternative to costly subscription services.
details: Meetily is a free, open-source application for Windows and macOS that transcribes and summarizes meetings using local AI models. It eliminates the need for expensive subscriptions and addresses privacy concerns by processing data on your device.

The tool works by recording both your microphone and system audio, allowing it to capture all sides of any conversation. This enables compatibility with all video conferencing platforms, including Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams.

During a meeting, users can watch the transcription in near real-time or minimize the window. Afterward, Meetily provides a full transcription and an AI-generated summary, with options to provide specific instructions for the summary's focus. It also supports processing previously recorded audio or video files.

The free version of Meetily has limitations, notably the absence of speaker labels, which can be a drawback for some users. Alternatives like noScribe offer speaker identification for file conversions, while Anarlog provides a different UI and access to various AI models.
caption:
